objects.description: Opaque parent-context type used by the talloc hierarchical allocator. It denotes that a pointer is a talloc context and can own children. Being typedef’d to void makes it opaque; treat it only as a handle to talloc-managed memory.

functions.name: talloc_version_major
functions.description: Returns the major version number of the talloc library. Useful for runtime version checks.

functions.name: talloc_version_minor
functions.description: Returns the minor version number of the talloc library. Useful for runtime version checks.

functions.name: talloc_test_get_magic
functions.description: Returns an internal magic value used by talloc tests. Intended primarily for testing/verification.

functions.name: _talloc
functions.description: Internal allocation function that creates a new talloc chunk of the given size under the specified parent context.
requirements: context may be NULL to create a top-level context
size may be 0 to create a zero-length context
Returned pointer is a talloc context and must be freed with talloc_free() or its wrappers

functions.name: talloc_init
functions.description: Creates a zero-length, named top-level talloc context. Name is formatted via printf-style arguments.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string if variadic arguments are provided
Returned pointer must be freed with talloc_free() to release the context and its children

functions.name: _talloc_free
functions.description: Internal free routine that frees a talloc chunk and all its children. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (e.g., destructor failure or multiple parents).
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by talloc (or compatible) or NULL
If ptr is NULL, no modification occurs and -1 is returned
If ptr has more than one parent, freeing is refused; use talloc_unlink() instead
If a destructor attached to ptr returns -1, free is aborted and -1 is returned

functions.name: talloc_free_children
functions.description: Frees all children of the given talloc context but not the context itself. No-op if ptr is NULL.
requirements: ptr should be a valid talloc context or NULL

functions.name: _talloc_set_destructor
functions.description: Assigns or removes a destructor on a talloc chunk. The destructor is called when the chunk is freed and should return 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
_destructor may be NULL to remove the current destructor
If the destructor attempts to talloc_free() its own ptr, the free will be ignored and talloc_free() returns -1

functions.name: _talloc_steal_loc
functions.signature: void *_talloc_steal_loc(const void *new_ctx, const void *ptr, const char *location);
functions.description: Changes the parent of a talloc chunk to new_ctx. Returns ptr. Internal variant that records call location.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
new_ctx may be NULL to reparent to top-level
If ptr has multiple parents, the current parent indicated by talloc_parent() is replaced; consider talloc_reparent() to disambiguate
Caller should avoid creating parent/child loops

functions.name: talloc_set_name
functions.description: Sets a human-readable name on a talloc chunk, allocating storage for the formatted string as a child of ptr.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string if variadic arguments are provided
Multiple calls allocate additional memory; all are freed when ptr is freed

functions.name: _talloc_move
functions.description: Moves a talloc chunk to a new parent and sets the source pointer (pointed-to by pptr) to NULL. Returns the moved pointer.
requirements: pptr must be a non-NULL pointer to a pointer previously allocated by talloc (or compatible)
new_ctx may be NULL to move to a top-level context

functions.name: talloc_set_name_const
functions.description: Sets a constant string as the name of a talloc chunk without allocating memory. Faster than talloc_set_name().
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
name must outlive ptr (must not reference transient memory)

functions.name: talloc_named
functions.signature: void *talloc_named(const void *context, size_t size, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Allocates a talloc chunk of given size as a child of context and assigns it a formatted name.
requirements: context may be NULL to allocate under the top-level context
size may be 0 to create a zero-length context
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string if variadic arguments are provided

functions.name: talloc_named_const
functions.signature: void *talloc_named_const(const void *context, size_t size, const char *name);
functions.description: Allocates a talloc chunk of given size as a child of context and assigns it the given constant name (no extra allocation for name).
requirements: context may be NULL
size may be 0
name should point to valid memory for the desired lifetime of the chunk name

functions.name: _talloc_zero
functions.signature: void *_talloc_zero(const void *ctx, size_t size, const char *name);
functions.description: Allocates a talloc chunk of given size under ctx and zero-initializes its contents. Assigns the provided name.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
size may be 0
name should be a valid string used for the talloc name

functions.name: talloc_get_name
functions.description: Returns the current name associated with a talloc chunk.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer

functions.name: talloc_check_name
functions.description: Checks whether a talloc chunk has the specified name; returns the pointer if it matches, otherwise NULL.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
name must be a valid string to compare against

functions.name: talloc_parent
functions.description: Returns the parent context of a talloc chunk, or NULL on error.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer

functions.name: talloc_parent_name
functions.description: Returns the name of the parent context of the given talloc chunk.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer

functions.name: talloc_total_size
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes used by a talloc chunk and all its descendants. Mostly for debugging.
requirements: ptr may be NULL; only meaningful if leak reporting has been enabled via talloc_enable_leak_report() or talloc_enable_leak_report_full()

functions.name: talloc_total_blocks
functions.description: Returns the total number of talloc blocks used by a chunk and all descendants. Mostly for debugging.
requirements: ptr may be NULL; only meaningful if leak reporting has been enabled via talloc_enable_leak_report() or talloc_enable_leak_report_full()

functions.name: _talloc_memdup
functions.signature: void *_talloc_memdup(const void *t, const void *p, size_t size, const char *name);
functions.description: Duplicates a raw memory region of length size into a new talloc chunk under t and assigns the provided name. Internal variant with explicit name.
requirements: t may be NULL to allocate at top-level
p must be non-NULL if size > 0
size is the number of bytes to copy

functions.name: _talloc_get_type_abort
functions.signature: void *_talloc_get_type_abort(const void *ptr, const char *name, const char *location);
functions.description: Asserts that the talloc chunk pointed to by ptr has the given type name; if not, calls the configured abort function. Returns ptr on success.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
name must be the expected type name string
Calling this may terminate the process if the check fails

functions.name: talloc_find_parent_byname
functions.description: Searches up the talloc hierarchy from ctx to find the nearest parent with the specified name. Returns that context or NULL.
requirements: ctx must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
name must be a valid string to match against

functions.name: _talloc_pooled_object
functions.signature: void *_talloc_pooled_object(const void *ctx, size_t type_size, const char *type_name, unsigned num_subobjects, size_t total_subobjects_size);
functions.description: Allocates an object of type_size bytes under ctx and equips it with an internal pool for its children, sized for num_subobjects and total_subobjects_size.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
type_size is the size of the main object
type_name is used for naming/debugging
num_subobjects indicates the expected number of child chunks (allocates header space)
total_subobjects_size is the total bytes anticipated for the children

functions.name: talloc_increase_ref_count
functions.description: Increases the reference count of a talloc chunk (equivalent to talloc_reference(NULL, ptr)).
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer

functions.name: talloc_reference_count
functions.description: Returns the number of references currently held to a talloc chunk.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer

functions.name: _talloc_reference_loc
functions.signature: void *_talloc_reference_loc(const void *context, const void *ptr, const char *location);
functions.description: Adds an additional parent reference from context to ptr and records call location. Returns ptr on success, NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: ptr may be NULL (no-op, returns NULL)
context must be a valid talloc context when adding a reference
Each additional reference consumes memory; avoid unnecessary graph-like structures

functions.name: talloc_unlink
functions.description: Removes a specific parent (context) from a talloc chunk’s parent set. Use to drop references or remove a direct parent.
requirements: context must be either a direct parent of ptr or a context used in talloc_reference() for ptr
ptr must be a talloc-managed pointer
Returns -1 if the specified parent has already been removed, or if ptr is NULL

functions.name: talloc_autofree_context
functions.description: Returns a talloc context that is automatically freed on program exit via atexit(). Intended to reduce leak-report noise.
requirements: Do not use in code that can be dlopen()/dlclose()’d due to atexit handler lifetime issues on some platforms

functions.name: talloc_get_size
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes allocated for this talloc chunk (excluding children). Useful for array-length calculations.
requirements: ctx must be a valid talloc chunk pointer

functions.name: talloc_show_parents
functions.description: Prints the ancestry of a talloc context to the given FILE stream.
requirements: context must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
file must be a valid FILE* (e.g., stdout, stderr, or an open file)

functions.name: talloc_is_parent
functions.description: Checks whether context appears in the ancestry (is a parent) of ptr in the talloc hierarchy. Returns 1 if true, 0 otherwise.
requirements: context and ptr must be valid talloc pointers

functions.name: talloc_reparent
functions.signature: void *talloc_reparent(const void *old_parent, const void *new_parent, const void *ptr);
functions.description: Changes a talloc chunk’s parent from old_parent to new_parent. Unlike talloc_steal(), it specifies which parent to change when multiple parents exist.
requirements: ptr must be a valid talloc chunk pointer
old_parent must be an existing parent of ptr
new_parent may be NULL to reparent to top-level

functions.name: _talloc_array
functions.signature: void *_talloc_array(const void *ctx, size_t el_size, unsigned count, const char *name);
functions.description: Allocates an array under ctx with count elements of size el_size and assigns the given name. Performs overflow-safe sizing via the talloc layer.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
count is the number of elements; may be 0
el_size must be the element size; product el_size*count must fit in size_t

functions.name: _talloc_zero_array
functions.signature: void *_talloc_zero_array(const void *ctx, size_t el_size, unsigned count, const char *name);
functions.description: Allocates a zero-initialized array under ctx with count elements of size el_size and assigns the given name.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
count may be 0
el_size must be the element size; product el_size*count must fit in size_t

functions.name: _talloc_realloc_array
functions.signature: void *_talloc_realloc_array(const void *ctx, void *ptr, size_t el_size, unsigned count, const char *name);
functions.description: Changes the size of a talloc-managed array to hold count elements of size el_size. Uses ctx only if ptr is NULL. Returns new pointer or NULL on error.
requirements: If ptr is NULL: behaves like allocation under ctx
If count is 0: behaves like talloc_free(ptr)
If ptr has more than one parent, the call fails
Product el_size*count must fit in size_t

functions.name: _talloc_realloc
functions.signature: void *_talloc_realloc(const void *context, void *ptr, size_t size, const char *name);
functions.description: Untyped reallocation of a talloc chunk to a new size. Uses context only if ptr is NULL. Returns new pointer or NULL on error.
requirements: If ptr is NULL: behaves like allocation under context of size bytes
If size is 0: behaves like talloc_free(ptr)
If ptr has more than one parent, the call fails

functions.name: talloc_realloc_fn
functions.description: Function version of talloc_realloc_size suitable for use as a realloc-like function pointer. Encapsulates malloc/free/realloc behavior within talloc.
requirements: If ptr is NULL: allocates under context
If size is 0: frees ptr
If ptr has multiple parents, resize fails

functions.name: talloc_strdup
functions.description: Duplicates a C string p into a new talloc chunk under t and sets the chunk name to the duplicated string.
requirements: t may be NULL
p must be a valid NUL-terminated string

functions.name: talloc_strdup_append
functions.description: Appends string a to talloc string s, reallocating s to fit. If s is NULL, a new context is created.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must be a talloc-managed NUL-terminated string
a must be a valid NUL-terminated string

functions.name: talloc_strdup_append_buffer
functions.description: Appends string a to talloc buffer s using the buffer’s allocated size (may differ from strlen). If s is NULL, a new context is created.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must be a talloc-managed buffer
a must be a valid NUL-terminated string
Be aware of embedded NULs in s; resulting logical string may differ from talloc_strdup_append()

functions.name: talloc_strndup
functions.signature: char *talloc_strndup(const void *t, const char *p, size_t n);
functions.description: Duplicates up to n bytes from string p into a new talloc chunk under t and sets the chunk name to the duplicated string.
requirements: t may be NULL
p must be a valid string pointer; up to n bytes are copied

functions.name: talloc_strndup_append
functions.description: Appends up to n bytes from string a to string s, reallocating s as needed. If s is NULL, a new context is created.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must be a talloc-managed NUL-terminated string
a must be a valid string pointer; up to n bytes are used

functions.name: talloc_strndup_append_buffer
functions.description: Appends up to n bytes from string a to buffer s using the buffer’s allocated size (not strlen). If s is NULL, a new context is created.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must be a talloc-managed buffer
a must be a valid string pointer; up to n bytes are appended
Be aware of embedded NULs in s; behavior differs from strndup_append()

functions.name: talloc_vasprintf
functions.signature: char *talloc_vasprintf(const void *t, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a string using fmt and ap into a new talloc chunk under t and sets the chunk name to the new string.
requirements: t may be NULL
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string
ap must be a valid va_list initialized for fmt

functions.name: talloc_vasprintf_append
functions.description: Appends a formatted string (fmt, ap) to talloc string s, reallocating as necessary. Sets name to the resulting string.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must be a talloc-managed NUL-terminated string
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string
ap must be a valid va_list initialized for fmt
If s is NULL, a new context is created

functions.name: talloc_vasprintf_append_buffer
functions.description: Appends a formatted string (fmt, ap) to talloc buffer s using allocated size rather than strlen. Sets name to the resulting string.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must be a talloc-managed buffer
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string
ap must be a valid va_list initialized for fmt
If s is NULL, a new context is created
Beware embedded NULs in s

functions.name: talloc_asprintf
functions.description: Formats a string using printf-style arguments into a new talloc chunk under t and sets the chunk name to the new string.
requirements: t may be NULL
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string

functions.name: talloc_asprintf_append
functions.description: Appends a formatted string to talloc string s, reallocating as necessary. Use when existing string may have been truncated.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must be a talloc-managed NUL-terminated string
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string
If s is NULL, a new context is created

functions.name: talloc_asprintf_append_buffer
functions.description: Appends a formatted string to talloc buffer s using the buffer’s allocated size. More efficient than talloc_asprintf_append() but differs with embedded NULs.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must be a talloc-managed buffer
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string
If s is NULL, a new context is created
Beware embedded NULs in s; behavior differs from asprintf_append()

functions.name: talloc_report_depth_cb
functions.signature: void talloc_report_depth_cb(const void *ptr, int depth, int max_depth, void (*callback)(const void *ptr, int depth, int max_depth, int is_ref, void *private_data), void *private_data);
functions.description: Walks the talloc tree rooted at ptr (or the top-level if ptr is NULL and leak reporting is enabled) and invokes callback for each node, up to max_depth.
requirements: Call with depth set to 0 for the initial call

f must be a valid FILE*
ptr may be NULL, but output for NULL requires leak reporting to be enabled

functions.name: talloc_report_full
functions.description: Recursively prints a detailed report of all memory referenced by ptr (or the top-level if ptr is NULL and leak reporting is enabled) to FILE f.
requirements: f must be a valid FILE*
ptr may be NULL; output for NULL requires leak reporting to be enabled

functions.name: talloc_report
functions.description: Prints a summary report of memory used by the immediate children of ptr (or the top-level if ptr is NULL and leak reporting is enabled) to FILE f.

functions.name: talloc_enable_null_tracking_no_autofree

functions.name: talloc_enable_leak_report_full
functions.description: Enables a full detailed leak report of the NULL context on program exit by calling talloc_report_full(NULL, stderr). Must be called before other talloc use.
requirements: Call before any other talloc use to establish the null context for complete reports

functions.name: talloc_set_abort_fn

requirements: abort_fn must be a valid function pointer and should not return (typically calls abort())

functions.description: Directs talloc log output to stderr using the built-in logger.

data_types.description: A C printf-compatible format string that may include conversion specifiers such as %s, %u, etc. In these stubs it is a fixed literal passed to functions like talloc_init, talloc_set_name, and talloc_named to format names.
An unconstrained NUL-terminated UTF-8/byte string used as general textual data or names. Obtained from FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and passed via c_str() to APIs expecting const char*.
Raw binary data buffer of arbitrary bytes used as a memory region (not necessarily NUL-terminated). Here provided by std::string::data() with an explicit length for duplication.
A path string referring to a file location on the local filesystem. In these stubs produced by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and used with fopen.
Arbitrary bytes stored in a file referenced by a provided path. The function under test writes output to this file via a FILE*; the specific content is not constrained and may be any data.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target dtype: printf-style format string arguments are fixed literals in stubs ("%s").
# The fuzzable inputs here are the strings passed as the %s argument (FUZZ_PARAM_STR) and
# sizes/flags come from FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int). Our buffer should therefore contain one or
# more NUL-terminated strings that are interesting as names, plus some 32-bit integers to
# seed size/flags when the harness reads them. We keep inputs valid: real C strings with
# terminating NULs and reasonable lengths.
#
# Layout we produce (all little-endian where integers appear):
# [u32 size_hint][u32 flag_bits]
# [name1 NUL][name2 NUL][name3 NUL] ... up to a cap, within 4096 bytes total
# The fuzzer harness typically consumes strings sequentially from the buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# and 32-bit integers for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int). By providing a variety of name strings
# (ASCII, UTF-8, long, short, with spaces, symbols, and embedded printf-like tokens that will be
# treated as plain data for %s) we exercise code paths without breaking the printf usage.

SAFE_MAX = 4096

WORDLIST_BASE = [
    "root",
    "ctx",
    "parent",
    "child",
    "alpha",
    "beta",
    "gamma",
    "δelta",
    "名前",
    "контекст",
    "spaced name",
    "tabs\tinside",
    "newline\ninside",
    "percent%literal",
    "braces{ }",
    "quotes\"\'",
    "path/like/name",
    "dot.name",
    "very-long-name-",
]

SYMBOLS = "-_ .:/@#%+={}[]()!$^,&" * 2


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789" + SYMBOLS
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))


def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some multi-byte code points
    s: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(length):
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.7:
            s.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1))
        elif t < 0.85:
            # Latin-1 supplement range (as unicode, encodes to 2 bytes in UTF-8)
            s.append(chr(r.randint(0x00A1, 0x00FF)))
        elif t < 0.95:
            # Greek, Cyrillic
            s.append(chr(r.randint(0x0370, 0x04FF)))
        else:
            # CJK common
            s.append(chr(r.randint(0x4E00, 0x9FFF)))
    return "".join(s)


def _interesting_sizes(r: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    # Bias toward small and boundary sizes used in stub (<= 2048)
    b = [0, 1, 2, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024, 1536, 2047, 2048]
    # Sprinkle a few random ones within range
    for _ in range(6):
        b.append(r.randint(0, 2048))
    return b


def _build_names(r: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    names: List[str] = []

    # Start with some curated entries
    base = WORDLIST_BASE.copy()
    r.shuffle(base)
    names.extend(base[:8])

    # Add boundary-length names
    names.append("")  # empty
    names.append("a")
    names.append("A" * 31)
    names.append("B" * 32)
    names.append("C" * 63)
    names.append("D" * 64)
    names.append("E" * 127)
    names.append("F" * 128)

    # Add mixed UTF-8 names
    names.append(_rand_utf8(r, r.randint(5, 20)))
    names.append(_rand_utf8(r, r.randint(20, 60)))

    # Add long composite name but keep within budget
    long_part = _rand_ascii(r, r.randint(200, 400))
    names.append("long-" + long_part)

    # Some with printf-looking content that will be inserted via %s safely
    names.append("literal-%s-here")
    names.append("num-%u-and-%d")
    names.append("mix-%p-%x-%o")

    # Random additional names
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            names.append(_rand_ascii(r, r.randint(3, 40)))
        else:
            names.append(_rand_utf8(r, r.randint(3, 40)))

    # Serialize with NUL terminators until budget
    out = bytearray()
    for s in names:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        if len(out) + len(b) > budget:
            break
        out += b
    # Ensure at least one name present
    if not out:
        out += b"default\x00"
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a size hint and flag bits for the stub's unsigned int params
    sizes = _interesting_sizes(r)
    size_hint = r.choice(sizes)

    # flag_bits: lowest bit toggles use_null_parent in talloc_named stub
    flag_bits = 0
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        flag_bits |= 1  # request NULL parent sometimes
    # Add some extra random bits to vary other FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) consumers
    flag_bits |= r.getrandbits(31) << 1

    header = struct.pack('<II', size_hint, flag_bits & 0xFFFFFFFF)

    # Remaining budget for names
    budget = max(0, SAFE_MAX - len(header))
    names_blob = _build_names(r, budget)

    return header + names_blob

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for FUZZ_PARAM_STR inputs used widely across talloc stubs.
# We craft a corpus of interesting strings and also synthesize additional
# ones based on the seed to cover names, format-like content, edge sizes,
# embedded NUL tails (not inside, since FUZZ_PARAM_STR() feeds c_str()),
# and various character classes.

def _base_corpus() -> List[bytes]:
    return [
        b"",  # empty name/string
        b"0", b"1", b"42",
        b"a", b"A", b"z", b"Z",
        b"talloc", b"context", b"name", b"fuzz-const-name",
        b"hello world",
        b"%s", b"%u", b"%p", b"%s-%u",
        b"samba-talloc",
        b"..", b".", b"/", b"\\",
        b"parent", b"child", b"root",
        b"alpha_beta-gamma.delta",
        b"0123456789",
        b"upperLOWERmix",
        b"with spaces   inside",
        b"unicode-\xe2\x98\x83",  # UTF-8 snowman
        b"longname-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",  # moderately long
        b"bin-\x00-trailer",  # has NUL after c_str() end but okay as storage
    ]

def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .:/\\%"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)).encode('utf-8')

def _random_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII with some multibyte UTF-8 sequences
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.75:
            parts.append(bytes([rng.choice(list(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_ .:/%"))]))
        else:
            # pick from a small set of valid UTF-8 sequences
            parts.append(rng.choice([
                "€".encode("utf-8"),
                "ß".encode("utf-8"),
                "ñ".encode("utf-8"),
                "中".encode("utf-8"),
                "🙂".encode("utf-8"),
            ]))
    return b"".join(parts)

def _sized_block(rng: random.Random, max_size: int) -> bytes:
    # For memdup and array payloads: return up to max_size arbitrary bytes
    n = rng.randint(0, max_size)
    return rng.randbytes(n)

def _compose_multiple(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Join with newlines, as FUZZ harness usually reads per-call slices; trailing NUL terminator will be added globally.
    return b"\n".join(strings)

# Layout strategy:
# The fuzzer framework typically splits a single input buffer into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() consumptions.
# We will pack a sequence of interesting strings separated by newlines. Callers will read them in order.
# Keep total under 4096 bytes.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    corpus = list(_base_corpus())

    # Seed-dependent additions to exercise various paths:
    # 1) Names for talloc_init/talloc_set_name etc.
    corpus.append(_random_ascii(rng, 0, 64))
    corpus.append(_random_utf8(rng, 1, 48))

    # 2) Strings with format-like content used by talloc_asprintf family
    corpus.append(("fmt-%s-%u-" + str(rng.randint(0, 9999))).encode("utf-8"))

    # 3) Very long but bounded names (ensure within 4k budget)
    long_len = rng.randint(256, 1024)
    corpus.append(("L" * long_len).encode("utf-8"))

    # 4) Binary-looking sources for _talloc_memdup size-bounded copies
    corpus.append(_sized_block(rng, 512))

    # 5) Strings likely to match literal checks like "fuzz-const-name"
    corpus.append(b"fuzz-const-name")

    # 6) Edge whitespace and punctuation
    corpus.append(b" \t leading and trailing \n ")

    # 7) Empty again to increase chance one consumer gets empty
    corpus.append(b"")

    # 8) Small numeric strings to feed into potential downstream parsing
    corpus.append(str(rng.randint(0, 1 << 31)).encode("ascii"))

    # 9) Type names for pooled object
    corpus.append(b"pooled-type-")

    # Ensure each segment is NUL-safe as C strings; embedded NULs are fine for storage but
    # c_str() will stop at first NUL. We keep them rarely to test buffer-append variants.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s = _random_ascii(rng, 5, 20) + b"\x00" + _random_ascii(rng, 5, 20)
        corpus.append(s)

    # Compose into a single buffer separated by newlines.
    buf = _compose_multiple(corpus)

    # Constrain to <= 4096 bytes. If oversized, trim from the end at a newline boundary if possible.
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        # Try to find a cut at or before 4096
        cut = buf.rfind(b"\n", 0, 4096)
        if cut == -1:
            buf = buf[:4096]
        else:
            buf = buf[:cut]

    # Add a final newline and NUL terminator to make it friendly to line-based consumers
    # and also suitable when read as a C-string block by the harness.
    if not buf.endswith(b"\n"):
        buf += b"\n"
    # NUL at end will be ignored by line-based, but safe for c_str uses.
    buf += b"\x00"

    return buf

import random
import struct
import itertools
from typing import List

# This generator targets talloc _talloc_memdup fuzzer stub where FUZZ_PARAM_STR provides:
# - source buffer bytes (may include NULs)
# - name string for the talloc chunk (printf-style names allowed but treated as raw C-string)
# Our goal: produce a single bytes buffer that the harness will split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_* calls.
# Assumptions commonly used by fuzzing harnesses:
# - Each FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumes a length-prefixed or delimiter-split segment from the provided buffer.
# - To maximize validity, we craft a buffer that includes two distinct string blobs with varied lengths/content
#   and sufficient size so that n (copy length) chosen by the stub will be <= src.size().
# Strategy:
# - Construct a composite buffer consisting of two length-prefixed strings using a simple internal format:
#   [u32 len1][bytes len1][u32 len2][bytes len2]
#   Many harnesses read raw strings directly, but if they instead slice sequentially, the raw bytes will still be
#   valid as arbitrary data; we keep sizes small and include multiple interesting patterns.
# - src (first string): include repeating patterns, ASCII text, embedded NULs, high-bit bytes.
# - name (second string): ASCII-friendly with printf tokens, UTF-8, long run, and final NUL to act as C-string terminator.
# - Total size kept <= 4096 bytes.
# - Randomness seeded via the provided seed parameter.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"alpha", b"beta", b"gamma", b"delta", b"epsilon",
    b"context", b"parent", b"child", b"talloc", b"memdup",
    b"zero\x00byte", b"embedded\x00nul", b"buffer", b"array", b"realloc",
]

PRINTF_TOKENS = [b"%s", b"%d", b"%u", b"%p", b"%zu", b"%ld", b"%%", b"%08x"]

HIGH_BYTES = bytes(range(128, 256))
LOW_BYTES = bytes(range(0, 128))


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_src(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build source with mixed segments to exercise memdup with arbitrary data.
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) ASCII words joined with separators (including NULs)
    words = rng.sample(ASCII_WORDS, k=rng.randint(3, min(8, len(ASCII_WORDS))))
    sep_options = [b" ", b"|", b",", b"\x00", b"/", b"::"]
    sep = rng.choice(sep_options)
    parts.append(sep.join(words))

    # 2) Repeated pattern blocks
    pattern = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(2, 8))
    repeat = rng.randint(1, 50)
    parts.append(pattern * repeat)

    # 3) Include a slice of high-bit bytes and low bytes with NULs sprinkled
    hb = HIGH_BYTES[: rng.randint(16, 64)]
    lb = LOW_BYTES[: rng.randint(16, 64)]
    parts.append(hb)
    # Sprinkle NULs
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        zeros = b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 16)
        insert_at = rng.randint(0, len(lb))
        lb = lb[:insert_at] + zeros + lb[insert_at:]
    parts.append(lb)

    # 4) Random chunk
    parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 128)))

    # 5) Optional empty to allow n==0 path
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(b"")

    src = b"".join(parts)

    # Clip to reasonable size for the stub (copy length limited to 2048 in stub)
    if len(src) > 3000:
        src = src[:3000]
    return src


def _make_name(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a printable name with mixed content. Ensure it is NUL-terminated somewhere to mimic C-strings
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Prefix with a base label
    base = rng.choice([b"ctx", b"node", b"chunk", b"object", b"buffer"])
    parts.append(base + b"-")

    # Add some printf tokens
    tokens = rng.sample(PRINTF_TOKENS, k=rng.randint(1, min(4, len(PRINTF_TOKENS))))
    parts.append(b"".join(tokens))

    # Add random ASCII and some UTF-8 bytes
    ascii_len = rng.randint(3, 20)
    ascii_bytes = bytes(rng.choice(range(32, 127)) for _ in range(ascii_len))
    parts.append(ascii_bytes)

    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        utf8_snippets = ["μ", "✓", "é", "長", "🚀"]
        chosen = rng.sample(utf8_snippets, k=rng.randint(1, 3))
        utf8 = "".join(chosen).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        parts.append(utf8)

    # Occasionally embed NULs before the final terminator to test name handling
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(b"\x00")

    # Final explicit NUL terminator to behave as a C-string safely
    parts.append(b"\x00")

    name = b"".join(parts)
    # Keep name modest in size
    if len(name) > 512:
        name = name[:512]
    return name


def _pack_u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("<I", n & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    src = _make_src(rng)
    name = _make_name(rng)

    # Compose as two length-prefixed strings to be robust to various FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers.
    # Even if the harness reads sequentially without lengths, the raw data is still valid arbitrary bytes.
    blob = _pack_u32(len(src)) + src + _pack_u32(len(name)) + name

    # Ensure total size constraint
    return blob[:MAX_TOTAL]

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: writable file contents
# The fuzzers open a path from FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() with mode "wb" and write reports to it.
# Therefore, the only requirement is that the file contents can be arbitrary and size-limited.
# To exercise different I/O paths, we generate buffers of varying sizes and byte patterns that
# are valid to write and may reveal boundary behaviors in stdio buffering and talloc reporting.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# A selection of interesting byte-pattern generators to vary write behavior

def pattern_repeating(byte: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([byte]) * length


def pattern_increment(start: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([(start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(length)])


def pattern_decrement(start: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([(start - i) & 0xFF for i in range(length)])


def pattern_alternating(a: int, b: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    arr = bytearray(length)
    for i in range(length):
        arr[i] = a if (i % 2 == 0) else b
    return bytes(arr)


def pattern_blocks(block_sizes: List[int], length: int) -> bytes:
    # Create blocks of zeroes and 0xFF of specified sizes cycling through
    out = bytearray()
    idx = 0
    toggle = False
    while len(out) < length:
        bs = block_sizes[idx % len(block_sizes)]
        bs = min(bs, length - len(out))
        out.extend(b"\xFF" * bs if toggle else b"\x00" * bs)
        toggle = not toggle
        idx += 1
    return bytes(out)


def pattern_random(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    return rng.randbytes(length)


def choose_sizes(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Sizes chosen to exercise stdio buffering boundaries and small/large writes
    interesting = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256,
                   511, 512, 1023, 1024, 2047, 2048, 3072, 4095, 4096]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        size = rng.choice(interesting)
    else:
        size = rng.randint(0, MAX_SIZE)
    # Ensure <= MAX_SIZE
    return min(size, MAX_SIZE)


def build_buffer(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    if size == 0:
        return b""

    generators = []
    # Heavier weight on random and alternating to produce varied data
    generators.extend([
        (lambda: pattern_random(rng, size), 3),
        (lambda: pattern_alternating(0x00, 0xFF, size), 2),
        (lambda: pattern_alternating(0x55, 0xAA, size), 2),
        (lambda: pattern_repeating(0x00, size), 1),
        (lambda: pattern_repeating(0xFF, size), 1),
        (lambda: pattern_repeating(0x20, size), 1),  # spaces
        (lambda: pattern_increment(rng.randrange(256), size), 1),
        (lambda: pattern_decrement(rng.randrange(256), size), 1),
        (lambda: pattern_blocks([1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32], size), 1),
    ])

    # Weighted choice
    total_w = sum(w for _, w in generators)
    pick = rng.randrange(total_w)
    acc = 0
    for gen, w in generators:
        acc += w
        if pick < acc:
            return gen()

    # Fallback (shouldn't happen)
    return pattern_random(rng, size)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Determine target size
    size = choose_sizes(rng)

    # Build primary payload
    payload = build_buffer(rng, size)

    # Occasionally prefix with a short header-like blob to vary early bytes
    # This is still arbitrary and valid for writing; it may create more diverse content.
    if size > 0 and rng.random() < 0.3:
        # Simple header: magic + length (little-endian), followed by payload truncated to fit
        magic = rng.choice([b"TAL0", b"DATA", b"BLOB", b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"])  # 4 bytes
        remaining = max(0, MAX_SIZE - len(magic) - 4)
        # Decide final size considering header
        target_total = min(len(magic) + 4 + len(payload), MAX_SIZE)
        body = payload[: target_total - len(magic) - 4]
        header = magic + struct.pack("<I", len(body))
        return header + body

    return payload
